screens.note: D2 iteration 3 (graph.ts's HOME_SCREEN_ID): the real ScreenSpec entry main.ink's hand-authored home_hub/calendar knots tag themselves with (ink.ts's emitMain), so the stage pane resolves the Home Hub instead of showing whatever real screen the player last stood on. Never a start screen (status is 'hub', not 'start', so screen_hub/the calendar never offer it) and never a DayInput.picked_location value (location 'home' is never town/forest/farm, and the calendar can only ever pick from start screens). ink.ts excludes this id from the generic per-screen world-file loop — the Home Hub's flow is hand-authored, not generated from a ScreenSpec — so it mints no world/*.ink file. Bank/decorate/satchel-triage (GDD: 'bank what fits the satchel, and decorate it') are D6's build; this entry only carries enough shape for the stage pane to show a real, honest 'you are home' screen — no exits, no NPCs, no items.

screens.name: Festival Grounds
screens.vibe: Where the run's build-up pays off
screens.note: RULED (Roc, 2026-07-30, review item D11): the access lock is REMOVED. The Festival Grounds can be visited from the start; the festival itself happens on the last day. That is a calendar event in the day/progression data, not a screen lock — so the design law (locks open by performing knowledge) needs no exception here. Open by default, but not a main screen: it carries a story-NPC slot at a reduced draw weight (tuning.json story_guarantee.rare_screens). Status is "reachable" rather than "start" (D2, 2026-08-01): 08-levels.md calls this screen "the final screen", never a day-opening pick, and "reachable" (bare, no gate) keeps it unlocked without offering it at day_start/the calendar.
